newsitem.title: GERMANY: Danzas splits German air, sea freight sales.
newsitem.headline: Danzas splits German air, sea freight sales.

text.p: Danzas said it has split air and sea freight sales in Germany to try to win more large clients.
Volker Oesau, the freight forwarder's intercontinental manager Germany, said Danzas had replaced mixed regional air and sea sales teams with two separate air and sea units.
These units had their own dedicated management and staff in 20 local offices, he told Reuters in an interview.
"The idea is to build up specialist knowledge. A single person cannot sell everything, it is more efficient with someone who knows air cargo, for example," he said.
"Before we concentrated on small and medium-sized shippers and had 80-90 percent of business with them," he added.
"Now we are analysing the needs of large clients for supply chain management. The main growth in the next couple of years will be with larger clients."
Danzas had also appointed a global logistics manager to co-ordinate intercontinental multi-modal freight projects.
Oesau said Danzas was seeing double-figure growth in intercontinental freight business at present.
Danzas had won new clients and increased business with existing customers as well as cut operating costs by 10-15 percent, he added.

After a loss in 1995, Danzas made a small profit on intercontinental freight turnover of more than 400 million marks in 1996, with revenue split fairly equally between air and sea freight. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
